iterations: one complete pool cycle per timed batch
hypothesis: Repeated one-cache reads may conceal a bandwidth advantage of ASTC. Distinct resident allocations traversed once per cycle can expose a useful crossover.
positive_criterion: For pool_size=64, ASTC GPU median per call <= 0.8 times own FP16 in every one of three sessions. This would justify a next experiment, not prove whole-model acceleration.
negative_criterion: For pool_size=64, ASTC GPU median per call > 1.05 times own FP16 in every one of three sessions. Otherwise inconclusive by this gate.
scope: Precompressed identical-value repeated-block traffic fixtures, different resident GPU allocations. Same v4 D64 kernel and fixed tile256 for both paths; no tile retuning, eviction command, encoder, append, model quality, or hardware-counter evidence. Large pool does not by itself prove a specific cache miss rate or DRAM bandwidth.
correctness: Existing seven path own-reference gates plus selected pool-slot/wraparound checks before timing. No timing interpretation on failed gate. Report pool memory and actual GPU allocated sizes.
